testedDecision: Which Stage 1 caregiver and environmental findings are safety hazards needing nursing follow-up versus normal caregiver warmth or expected infant development.
reason: The Stage 3 teach-back enumerates corrections for the rear-facing seat, crib sleep, diphenhydramine, hot dogs, stair gates and cabinet locks, restating six keyed hazards as a checklist. Stage 2 confirms the cosmetics pouch holds an uncapped acetaminophen bottle, removing the inference that an unlocked pouch is itself a poisoning hazard. Nothing in the later stages flags maternal warmth or stranger anxiety, which also eliminates the reassuring distractor segments.

testedDecision: Interpret the clustered unsafe infant-care practices as caregiver knowledge deficit rather than neglect, willful disregard, or infant developmental delay.
reason: Stage 2 has Danielle tearfully saying nobody taught her how to do these things and describes aging out of foster care without support, which states the keyed knowledge-deficit reading almost verbatim. Stage 2 also reports the partner has not harmed Liam and leaves the room, defusing the intentional-neglect option. Stage 3 then shows her correcting nearly every practice after a single teaching session, which discriminates knowledge deficit from willful disregard.

testedDecision: Select nonjudgmental strengths-based teaching methods suited to a tearful isolated caregiver while still prioritizing and delivering urgent infant safety instruction today.
reason: Stage 3 narrates the nurse actually delivering structured teaching, written materials, community resources and a one-month follow-up appointment, naming three of the four keyed approaches outright. Danielle correctly restating each instruction displays teach-back as the method already chosen. Seeing that safety topics were in fact covered that day also removes the distractor of deferring teaching because she is crying.

testedDecision: Choose nursing actions for a reported tablespoon acetaminophen overdose, spanning exposure history, escalation, possible labs, measurement correction, and safe medication storage.
reason: Stage 3 shows Danielle stating she will use the supplied syringe and give the smaller correct volume, presenting the keyed syringe teaching and return demonstration as an accomplished fact. The Poison Control magnet handed over in Stage 3 cues the two keyed options that route escalation through Poison Control. A scheduled follow-up appointment further undercuts the lone distractor claiming no follow-up is needed because Liam looks well.
